Test case for {@link SequenceReader}.

A minimal {@link Reader} that tracks whether it has been closed and that always reports end-of-stream. Reading from it both verifies that the reader is still open and immediately closes it, so it doubles as a probe for confirming that {@link SequenceReader} closes the readers it drains.
The NUL character left behind in the untouched slots of a char buffer.
How many extra reads to perform when asserting a reader stays at end-of-stream.
Asserts that {@code actual} starts with exactly the characters in {@code expected}.
Asserts that reading the given reader one character at a time yields the characters of {@code expected} in order.
Asserts that the reader is exhausted: every further read returns EOF, and it stays at EOF across repeated reads.
emptyReader is exhausted immediately; singleCharReader yields one 'A' then EOF.
Both wrapped readers must be closed once the sequence has been fully drained.
"Foo" and "Bar" should be read back as a single continuous "FooBar".
A single read never crosses a reader boundary, so it stops at the end of "Foo".
Read "Foo" into the buffer starting at offset 3.
Read "Bar" into the buffer starting at offset 0, overwriting the leading NULs.
Out-of-bounds and null buffers must be rejected.
Pass the readers via the Iterable constructor overload.
A sequence of empty readers behaves as a single empty reader.
